# Coeleo OS

> Coeleo OS is a from-scratch x86_64 operating system written in Rust: its own kernel, syscall ABI, software compositor, shell and userspace, built in a single repository. It is not a Linux distribution and does not use the Linux kernel.

## Overview

- Target: x86_64, single core, ~512 MiB RAM, software linear framebuffer, no 3D GPU.
- Boot: Limine, on UEFI and legacy BIOS.
- Kernel: one Rust crate, folders by domain, no userspace code linked in.
- Userspace: static no_std ELFs (x86_64-unknown-none) that enter at _start.
- Syscall ABI: 27 syscalls, reached through the libcoeleo wrappers - the only crossing between rings.
- Process model: preemptive round-robin on a 100 Hz LAPIC tick, at most 8 concurrent processes, one thread per process.
- Memory: physical frame bitmap, 4-level paging with strict user/kernel isolation, kernel heap allocator.
- Storage: FAT32 with cluster allocation and long filenames, over VirtIO-blk, SATA AHCI (GPT) or USB Mass Storage.
- Network: smoltcp over virtio-net or Intel e1000e, static IPv4 or DHCP, ARP, ICMP echo, DNS A, HTTP client, TLS 1.2/1.3 via rustls.
- Packages: .coe payloads with Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 integrity verification.
- License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.

## What it is not

- Not a Linux distribution and not Unix-compatible: no libc, no dynamic linking, no POSIX ABI.
- Not derived from Redox, Windows, or an RTOS.
- No SMP, no threads, no Wi-Fi, no audio, no suspend, no 3D acceleration today.

## Build and run

- Host: Linux with QEMU, make, xorriso, python3, mtools and gdisk.
- make all - kernel ISO plus userspace ELFs and test packages.
- make run - UEFI boot with virtio-blk, virtio-net and a USB mouse.
- Other targets: make run-ahci, run-e1000e, run-usb, run-bios, run-hdd.
- Tests run QEMU headless and assert against the serial log.

## Reused components

- Limine - bootloader (UEFI and BIOS).
- Flanterm - terminal emulation.
- smoltcp - TCP/IP stack.
- fatfs - FAT32 filesystem.
- rustls - TLS 1.2/1.3.
- Everything else (memory, scheduler, compositor, syscalls, shell, UI toolkit, installer, package manager) is implemented in the repository.
